Ratu Sir Kamisese Mara was a high chief of Lau who led Fiji to independence on 10 October 1970 and served as prime minister until 1992, then as president until 2000.

Educated in New Zealand and at Oxford, he led the Alliance Party, which sought a balance between indigenous Fijians and Indo-Fijians. He made Fiji a leading voice of the Pacific states.

His party lost the 1987 election, and the coups that followed brought him back to power. In 2000 he was pushed out during the George Speight coup. He is remembered as the father of the nation, alongside Cakobau before him and the chiefs he led.
